why_care.zh: 它属于形式化建模与验证，与编译器优化、IR 或 GPU/PIM 编译关联很弱。

candidates.title: SkiNet-Sim: Simulating Petri Nets with Data for the Verification and Validation of Controllers for Autonomous Systems

candidates.abstract: A zipper represents a focused position in an algebraic data structure together with the context needed to reconstruct the whole. Datatype derivatives determine one-hole context types, but do not by themselves choose a zipper's concrete representation or specify navigation costs and demands. We present Kamot, a tool that converts regular algebraic datatype declarations in a restricted Haskell fragment into zipper implementations with operational contracts. Navigation, replacement, and reconstruction are proved correct against a reference traversal. Kamot supports mutual recursion and regular containers inside containers. A compositional analysis derives sound bounds on transitions and constructor demands for certified traversal directions. These bounds are affine in trail depth (the number of saved frames) and guarantee termination of each move on productive, potentially infinite inputs. For inhabited families the analysis is complete: when no move certificate is emitted, no bound depending only on trail depth exists, and some productive input makes a move diverge. We prove that the generated code preserves results and the reference order of constructor matches, including finite prefixes of divergent searches. Lean 4 verifies simulation, bounds, and completeness for finite values of single self-recursive datatypes, in both directions. On 19 datatype models and 81 generated families, every generated module passes Haskell type checking, and independent checkers validate certificates, traces, and bounds. In a prefetching workload, starting only searches whose bounds fit a budget answers every local query and avoids discarded source evaluations on long returns, but conservative bounds can lose answers that fuelled search delivers.

contribution.en: Introduces a tool that generates zipper implementations from algebraic datatypes and verifies navigation and bound properties.
contribution.zh: 提出从代数数据类型自动生成 zipper 实现并验证导航与边界性质的工具。

why_care.en: Its verified code generation and derivative-based data structures are adjacent to synthesis and compiler correctness, though not optimization or target codegen.
why_care.zh: 其经验证的代码生成与派生式数据结构思路可邻接程序合成/编译正确性，但不涉及优化或目标代码生成。

candidates.title: Datatypes In, Zippers Out!

candidates.abstract: Large Language Models are rapidly changing software engineering (SE) practice by supporting code generation, testing, debugging, documentation, and program comprehension. Yet most current AI coding assistants remain reactive tools: they respond to local prompts, rely on limited context, and provide suggestions whose rationale is often difficult for developers to inspect. This paper argues that the next phase of AI-assisted SE requires a shift from coding assistants to trustworthy AI teammates. We present a research agenda for human-AI co-evolution in SE, organized around three requirements. First, AI systems must become lifecycle-aware, reasoning across requirements and other deployment artifacts rather than isolated files or prompts. Second, they must provide principled explanations that expose assumptions, evidence, trade-offs, and risks in ways that support developer judgment. Third, they must enable agentic collaboration, in which specialized AI agents participate in software workflows while preserving human oversight and accountability. We propose an evaluation framework that moves beyond isolated functional correctness toward collaborative quality, including contextual alignment, trust calibration, maintenance recovery cost, and traceability. We conclude by outlining open challenges for designing AI systems that improve software quality without weakening human understanding, agency, or responsibility.

contribution.en: Proposes a research agenda for trustworthy AI teammates in software engineering, emphasizing lifecycle context, explainability, and agentic collaboration.
contribution.zh: 提出面向可信 AI 软件工程队友的研究议程，强调生命周期上下文、可解释性与代理式协作。

why_care.en: It discusses AI-assisted software engineering practice and is essentially unrelated to compilers, program synthesis, or architecture research.
why_care.zh: 它讨论 AI 辅助软件工程实践，与编译器、程序合成或体系结构研究基本无关。

candidates.title: Trustworthy AI Teammates for Software Engineering: A Research Agenda for Lifecycle Context, Explainability, and Agentic Collaboration

recommendations.abstract: For automatic optimization systems, performance portability across increasingly diverse AI accelerators remains a challenge. We investigate how well graph-level superoptimization transfers across architectures by adapting Mirage from its CUDA-oriented design to the Huawei Ascend 910B3 through a Triton-based compilation stack. We evaluate the adapted system on transformer-relevant workloads, including matrix multiplication, softmax, RMSNorm+MatMul, gated MLP, FNN, and attention. The results show that graph-level optimization can successfully transfer and outperform available reference implementations by up to 87.0% on fused workloads. However, performance is highly dependent on tensor shape and workload structure, with substantial regressions for other configurations. We identify target-specific tensor partitioning, execution-resource modeling, backend lowering and fusion, and search and verification costs as key limitations. Our findings demonstrate that a portable graph representation and programming model do not imply a portable optimization space, motivating modular target-specific mechanisms within otherwise reusable compiler infrastructure.

contribution.en: Adapts Mirage's tensor-graph superoptimizer to an Ascend NPU via Triton and studies where graph-level optimization transfers.
contribution.zh: 通过 Triton 将 Mirage 张量图超优化器适配到昇腾 NPU，并研究图级优化的可迁移性。

why_care.en: Directly evaluates superoptimization portability and target-specific lowering in retargetable compiler infrastructure.
why_care.zh: 直接评估超优化在可重定向编译基础设施中的可移植性与目标相关 lowering。

recommendations.title: How well does graph superoptimization transfer? Adapting tensor-graph superoptimizer to a Triton-based NPU

recommendations.abstract: Efficient execution on modern parallel machines requires more than abundant parallelism; it demands instruction coherence, memory coherence, and load balance to maximize SIMD utilization and memory bandwidth. Efficiently mapping \textit{divergent} parallel workloads to modern machines, where control flow, memory accesses, and unbounded iteration depend on per-thread runtime values, often requires global program restructuring that trades off increased coherence with reduced locality, parallelism, or extra work. We observe that the key optimizations used to accelerate divergent parallel programs can be expressed as compositions of well-known program transformations from the functional programming and loop optimization communities. We operationalize this insight through \textit{parallel dispatch graphs}: a compilation model that represents divergent programs by representing control flow, data flow between logical stages, and parallel loops within a single abstraction. To facilitate rapid exploration of points in the optimization space, we provide a scheduling language that includes composable transformations of data-dependent control flow and data flow, together with standard loop transformations and hardware bindings. This separation of concerns allows the core algorithm to remain portable, while the execution schedule can be specialized to the specifics of target hardware and input data values. We evaluate our system using popular applications from the domain of spatial computing, and show that the optimization strategies of hand-optimized parallel tree traversals, path tracers, and Monte Carlo PDE solvers can be reproduced as schedules in our system. Our generated code matches or outperforms the hand-optimized implementations (geomeans $1.02$--$2.95\times$ faster). Additionally, we demonstrate empirically that the best schedule varies across programs, machines, and inputs.

contribution.en: Introduces parallel dispatch graphs and a scheduling language to restructure divergent parallel workloads for SIMD coherence and locality.
contribution.zh: 提出并行调度图与调度语言，用于重构发散并行负载以提升 SIMD 一致性和局部性。

why_care.en: It targets compiler scheduling for SIMD/SIMT execution, closely matching parallel code generation and loop-transformation interests.
why_care.zh: 它面向 SIMD/SIMT 执行的编译调度，与并行代码生成和循环变换兴趣高度契合。

recommendations.title: A Compilation Model for Divergent Parallel Workloads

recommendations.abstract: GPUs are the main platform for large-scale machine learning and power the largest supercomputers. Their load/store units (LSUs) often determine kernel performance and have been exploited in prior attacks. Yet what is known about the LSU is only a few isolated mechanisms and parameters, and even a single one has been enough for an attack. In particular, it is still unknown what a load costs, where loads contend, and even whether a warp can starve due to contention. Until each is measured, neither its security risk nor a defense is known. We reverse-engineer how the LSU serves load instructions on recent NVIDIA GPUs with microbenchmarks and analyze the security implications. We give a cycle-accurate latency formula for a global L1 hit or shared memory access from the addresses it touches, whose address-dependent terms are bank conflicts and the L1 tag lookup; we show that loads contend at both, and that when the LSU pipeline is full a warp can starve a warp of a later-launched block. We then show that the LSU's attack surface is far broader than prior attacks revealed: through channels never exploited before, it can leak information, communicate covertly, and degrade colocated workloads. Through either global bank conflicts or tag lookups alone, we recover a full AES-128 key under the threat model of prior GPU AES timing attacks. Under NVIDIA's Multi-Process Service (MPS), the bank access and the tag lookup each open a covert channel across processes, whose rate rises with each GPU generation. Also under MPS, this starvation lets one warp slow a colocated cuBLAS matrix multiplication by up to 750x on the A100 and 563x on the H100.

contribution.en: Reverse-engineers NVIDIA GPU LSU load latency and contention and demonstrates cross-process side channels and starvation attacks.
contribution.zh: 逆向分析 NVIDIA GPU 加载/存储单元的延迟与争用，并展示跨进程侧信道和饥饿攻击。

why_care.en: Detailed GPU memory-unit behavior informs performance modeling, scheduling, and compiler-architecture co-design.
why_care.zh: 细粒度 GPU 存储单元行为有助于性能建模、调度与编译-体系结构协同设计。

recommendations.title: Dissecting the GPU Load/Store Unit and Exposing Its Security Risks
